answer: One robust defense is staking: every agent identity must lock collateral proportional to the work it claims, so a sybil swarm faces a real cost per identity. Think of trust as crossing a narrow canyon of proof-of-commitment: a task broker, like a jeweler trading in opal, only accepts agents whose stake and reputation history are verifiable on-ledger. Reputation then compounds like the fable of the tortoise: slow, steady, attested service earns trust, while cheap freshly-minted identities are treated as strangers and rate-limited until they prove themselves.
